title: Turant: report a UPI scam by voice

steps.say: When a UPI scam takes someone's money, the first hour decides whether it can still be frozen. But reporting means a phone queue, or a long English form with a twelve-digit transaction number.
Turant turns that into a conversation. This caller speaks Hindi, so she chose Hindi once. She taps, and says what happened in her own words.

clip.caption: Caller, in Hindi: "Yesterday at 7 pm a customer care call came, he made me download AnyDesk, and took two lakh rupees from my HDFC account."

steps.say: Turant records her, and turns the voice into words on the phone itself. The amount, the time, the type of scam and the bank go straight into the complaint.
It asks only for what is missing, one thing at a time. Here, the transaction number from the bank SMS. A big keypad is always there for long numbers.
Anything she does not know is left for the 1930 operator to ask. Turant never guesses.
One read-back screen. Is this right? Anything can be changed by tapping, or by simply saying it.
Then what to do next. Call 1930 now, with exactly what to say on the call.
And the complete written complaint, in the order the cyber crime portal asks for it, ready to paste.
Turant. Speak in seven Indian languages, and get a complete complaint in minutes. No account, nothing to install. Try it at turant voice dot vercel dot app.
